doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Day jobs, street playing and being attacked in the second month
summary: He washed dishes and played on the street; in his second month a stranger threw him through a window, and as a tourist he got free surgery.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That is a great story. That’s called paying dues. How did you make, when you were here those nine years, you had a day job or were you playing also?
Yeah, I had a day job, a dishwasher or getting ready for the lunchbox. And I played the street too.
You had a tough incident when you first arrived.

After a jam session, and I just bought a hamburger at Burger King and was walking. The first five months I was living at a hotel near Times Square. And some guy with two girls was screaming at me and dragged me around and threw me. And I had three stitches.
He threw you through a window?

Yeah. Three stitches. And no reason. He didn’t pick up my wallet or my wrist watch. Maybe he thought I was somebody he knew that he didn’t like. I don’t know. And the police came. But the good news is within three months, still I am a tourist. So they were very aware and they brought me to a hospital and did surgery, everything for free.
Yeah, yeah. Just the second month.
